name: cytoscape-web-app-examples
//workspaces: packages/* holds the SDK, which is NOT an app: it has no federation name,
no port, and no entry in apps.manifest.json. scripts/manifest.mjs filters
it out of the app-set comparison rather than the manifest gaining a second

//build: The SDK builds first and explicitly. Apps consume its dist/, so an
ordering that happens to work is not good enough — a fresh clone would
fail on whichever app npm decided to visit first.
scripts.build: npm run build:sdk && npm run build:apps
scripts.build:sdk: npm run build -w @cytoscape-web/app-runtime && npm run build -w create-cytoscape-app
scripts.build:apps: npm run build -w hello-world -w network-statistics -w network-workflows -w project-template
scripts.clean: rm -rf hello-world/dist network-statistics/dist network-workflows/dist project-template/dist packages/app-runtime/dist packages/create-cytoscape-app/dist packages/create-cytoscape-app/templates
scripts.rebuild: npm run clean && npm run build
scripts.deploy: npm run build && npm run copy-dist

//peerDependencies: Removed. This block used to be the repository's ONLY direct declaration of
@mui/material, react and react-dom — every app resolved them by hoisting.
Each app now declares its own peerDependencies (the packages the host
provides as Module Federation singletons), so there is nothing left for a
root block to supply. scripts/manifest.mjs cross-checks each app's ranges
//devDependencies: The build tooling here is only what the ROOT scripts need: Playwright for
the host preflight, and the shared TypeScript. Each app declares its own
vite, @module-federation/*, React and MUI, so a copied-out app installs on
its own — which is the documented way to start a new app.
